source_refs.note: Elimination of Urine: a main subheading of 14.1.3 Functioning of Kidney, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 16-17.

blocks.text: From the collecting ducts, urine flows through the renal pelvis into a ureter. Ureter leads to the urinary bladder. Muscular contractions of the bladder force urine out of the body through urethra. A normal adult eliminates from 1 to 2 L of urine a day. This amount is highly variable and depends on several factors. The more water or hydrating fluids we consume, the higher is the urine output. Diets with high salt trigger water retention and decrease urine production. Physical exercise leads to water loss through respiration and perspiration, which generally decreases urine volume.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: In hot weather, the body loses more water through sweat, leading the kidneys to conserve water and produce a smaller volume of concentrated urine.
